narrative.overview: A dark, precise, modern software-studio surface where every colored thing means something. Near-black ground, quiet panels separated by hairlines, calm generous type, and exactly two accents carrying the studio's two halves: green for listening (the conversation, understanding) and blue for building (the system, the action). Nothing is colored for decoration. Chosen by the user from three working comps after four rejected worlds, then restructured so the page progresses claim → what → proof → how → who → ask instead of restating one idea.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with quiet panels and hairline separation; no glow, neon, or gradient wash
Clash Display headlines over Switzer body
Green = listening, blue = building; the two accents never swap roles
No fabricated proof; Work renders only when real case studies exist

rules.name: The Two Halves Rule
rules.body: Green means listening/understanding; blue means building/acting. An accent that can't be assigned to one of those halves shouldn't be colored at all.

rules.name: The Fill Rule
rules.body: White text only on Volt Deep or darker. Live and bright Volt take dark text when filled, never white.

dos: Do keep every claim true today; the Work section renders only when a case-study file exists.
Do keep the email reachable in the first viewport and again at the close, with subject prefill and a copy button.
Do give every interactive element a hover state and a visible keyboard focus ring.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: reveals render settled.
donts: Don't put white text on Live or bright Volt.
Don't add a third accent, glows, neon edges, or decorative gradients; the method bar is the only gradient.
Don't restate a section's idea in another section, or end the page on anything but the ask.
Don't number sections other than the method steps.
